name: build-toolchain-pins
body: Every toolchain that compiles or stages a frontend is pinned to an exact version in a repo-visible, build-enforced place, so a release is reproducible. CI (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) already pins JDK 21 (`actions/setup-java`) and .NET 10.0.x (`actions/setup-dotnet`), but leaves Go, Node/npm, and the Rust compiler floating: `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, the runner-preinstalled `go`, and apt-installed `nodejs`/`npm`. The pin consumers are the paths that actually build: the CI release build — the `linux` job (`cargo build --release`, which drives `build.rs`) and the `bottle` job (which builds through the split Homebrew formulae) — plus those split formulae themselves (`apg-go` depends on `go`, `apg-ts` on `node`, `apg-rust`/`apg-py`/`apg-md` on `rust`), each of which builds one frontend directly. They must consume the same pins rather than a floating latest. `install.sh` is download-only — it fetches prebuilt release tarballs and never builds a frontend — so it consumes no toolchain and is not a pin consumer. Acceptance: `release.yml` names an exact Go version, an exact Node version, and an exact Rust toolchain; both CI build jobs and the per-language formulae resolve to the same versions; the pins are documented.
